plants.sentence: Sample size and standard error are unrelated: increasing the sample size leaves the variability of the sampling distribution unchanged.
Values inside a confidence interval are guaranteed to include the true population value, and every value outside it is certainly wrong.
Every properly constructed 95% confidence interval captures the parameter; only intervals built with mistakes ever miss it.
The variability of a sample statistic decreases with the square root of the sample size: a sample twice as large cuts the margin of error in half.

Bootstrapping, introduced by Bradley Efron in 1979, is a resampling procedure that uses the data from one sample to generate a sampling distribution, by repeatedly taking random samples from that sample.
In one example, working with the consultant caused patients' complication probability to fall to between 0% and 11.3%, as 95% of 10,000 bootstrap proportions showed.
